name: The Outer Reach
description: Frontier planets at the edge of a collapsed galactic government. Smugglers, bounty hunters, and settlers carving lives in the lawless expanse.
seed_prompt: A space western where frontier planets exist beyond the reach of a fractured galactic government, filled with smugglers, bounty hunters, and settlers building new lives.
lore_content:
The Alliance collapsed eighteen years ago. The core worlds still pretend to govern, but out here — past the Drift, where the beacon network ends — it's just ships, grit, and the cold math of survival. The Outer Reach is a string of colony worlds connected by trade routes that only the brave or desperate fly.

Captain Josie Malone runs the Jackrabbit, a modified cargo hauler that's seen better decades. She takes any job that pays and only asks questions when they're relevant to getting paid. Former Alliance military, she left after the Collapse and hasn't looked back. Her crew is family, her ship is home, and she'll burn anyone who threatens either.

Marshal Kade Vasquez is the last Alliance lawman in the Reach. His jurisdiction covers six planets and he has no backup, no warrant authority, and no illusions. He enforces what he can, lets go what he must, and drinks alone in port bars between jobs. He's looking for a fugitive war criminal named Harlow. Finding Harlow might kill him. Not finding Harlow definitely will.

The Combine is what passes for organized crime in the Reach — a loose federation of smuggling operations, protection rackets, and mining claims run by Boss Catarina Zheng from her flagship, the Iron Fortune. She's fair in her dealings, merciless to betrayers, and provides the only stable economy some of these colonies have. Several settlements would collapse without her supply runs.

Doc Okafor runs the clinic on Dust, the largest settlement in the Reach. He was a trauma surgeon on a core-world hospital station before the Collapse stranded him. He patches up gunshot wounds, delivers babies, and performs surgery with whatever's available. His waiting room always has people in it.

The Architects left ruins on every planet in the Reach — massive structures of an unknown alloy that resist every attempt at analysis. Most colonists ignore them. Some loot them for tradeable artifacts. A few have noticed that the ruins on different planets seem to be pointing at the same coordinates in deep space. Nobody wants to be the first to fly there.

Settlement Elara is the newest colony, three hundred souls trying to farm a planet that doesn't want them. Their water table is contaminated, their crops keep failing, and something in the mountains broadcasts a signal that scrambles electronics within five miles. They need help. They can't afford to pay for it.

origins.name: Colony-Born
origins.description: Raised on a Reach world, you know what it means to build something from nothing.
traits: Jury-Rigger: Proficiency with tinker's tools. You can repair broken equipment with improvised materials.

origins.name: Ex-Alliance
origins.description: You served the old government. Now you serve yourself. The skills remained; the loyalty expired.
traits: Military Training: Proficiency with all firearms and pilot's tools.
Alliance Codes: You can access old Alliance systems and channels (where they still function).

origins.name: Ship Rat
origins.description: Born on a ship, raised in the void. Dirt-side feels wrong to you.
traits: Spacer: You operate normally in zero gravity and can hold your breath for twice as long in vacuum.
Ship Sense: Advantage on checks to operate, repair, or navigate spacecraft.

origins.name: Drifter
origins.description: No home, no crew, no plan. Just you, the black, and whatever comes next.
traits: Quick Friends: You can establish a rapport with strangers quickly. Advantage on first Charisma checks with new people.
Wanderer's Luck: Once per long rest, you can reroll any one d20 roll.

archetypes.name: Ship Captain
archetypes.description: Your ship is your world. Keep it flying, keep the crew fed, and try not to die.

features.name: Rally the Crew
features.description: As a bonus action, give an order. One ally within 30 feet gains advantage on their next attack roll or saving throw.

features.name: Captain's Luck
features.description: When your ship takes damage or faces a critical malfunction, you can make a DC 15 Charisma check to mitigate the worst of it.

archetypes.name: Bounty Hunter
archetypes.description: You find people who don't want to be found. The pay is good. The danger is better.

features.name: Mark Target
features.description: Choose one creature as your quarry. You have advantage on Perception and Survival checks to track them, and deal an extra 1d6 damage on your first hit against them each turn.

features.name: No Escape
features.description: When your quarry attempts to flee, you can use your reaction to make an opportunity attack or move up to half your speed toward them.

archetypes.name: Ship Mechanic
archetypes.description: You keep the lights on and the engines burning. Without you, everyone dies in the cold dark.

features.name: Miracle Fix
features.description: Once per short rest, you can repair a broken device or weapon in 1 minute using improvised materials.

features.name: Booby Trap
features.description: Given 10 minutes and materials, you can rig a door, container, or piece of equipment to shock, alarm, or explode when tampered with.

archetypes.name: Frontier Medic
archetypes.description: Out here, you're the hospital. Make it count.

features.name: Triage
features.description: As an action, stabilize a dying creature and restore 1d8 + Wisdom modifier hit points.

features.name: Calm Under Pressure
features.description: You have advantage on Medicine checks made during combat or crisis situations.

setting_skills.name: Piloting
setting_skills.description: Flying spacecraft through hazardous conditions, docking maneuvers, and evasive action.

setting_skills.name: Ship Systems
setting_skills.description: Understanding, repairing, and modifying spacecraft systems and components.

setting_skills.name: Underworld Contacts
setting_skills.description: Connections to smuggling networks, fences, and information brokers across the Reach.

setting_skills.name: Architect Lore
setting_skills.description: Knowledge of the mysterious Architect ruins found across Reach worlds.

world_descriptors.architecture: Frontier settlements built from salvaged ship parts and local materials, the Jackrabbit's worn but functional interior, Doc Okafor's clinic cobbled together from pre-Collapse equipment, Iron Fortune's imposing bulk, Architect ruins of unknown alloy pointing at something in deep space, Settlement Elara's struggling prefab structures
world_descriptors.landscape: Dusty frontier worlds under harsh suns, the endless black between colonies, mysterious Architect ruins on every planet, Dust's sprawling settlement visible from orbit, the mountains near Elara broadcasting strange signals, asteroid fields hiding smuggler routes
world_descriptors.vegetation: Hardy crops struggling in alien soil, hydroponic systems aboard ships, whatever native flora each colony world offers, the strange growth patterns near Architect ruins, community gardens in established settlements
world_descriptors.weather: Dust storms on frontier worlds, the artificial climate of ship interiors, contaminated water tables, electromagnetic interference near Elara's mountains, the unforgiving vacuum of space, harsh sunlight on worlds with thin atmospheres
world_descriptors.people: Captain Josie Malone weathered by hard years, Marshal Vasquez alone against impossible odds, Boss Zheng commanding respect, Doc Okafor exhausted but dedicated, colonists building lives from nothing, bounty hunters tracking fugitives across multiple worlds
world_descriptors.clothing: Flight jackets worn soft from use, practical frontier wear in dusty earth tones, Combine enforcers in matching gear, medical coats stained with work, Marshal's badge tarnished but polished, mechanic coveralls covered in engine grease
world_descriptors.technology: Modified cargo haulers held together by skill and prayer, frontier medical equipment making do with what's available, the broken beacon network at the edge of known space, Architect artifacts no one understands, jury-rigged everything, weapons well-maintained because they have to be
world_descriptors.lighting: Harsh alien sunlight on settlement streets, the warm amber of ship interiors, cold stars visible through viewports, the eerie glow of Architect ruins, flickering power in struggling colonies, the red warning lights of system alerts

visual_identity.visual_exclusions: Clean high-tech aesthetics, military discipline and polish, urban environments, large populations, luxury or abundance, stable government presence
